utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could we have the case called, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is case number IT-04-79-PT, The Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the record, the representation. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Alan Tieger, Anna Richterova, and Karen Bose appearing for the Prosecution, with case manager Wilhelmus Wijermars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, Stevo Bezbradica, counsel for the accused, Mr. Mico Stanisic, and my co-counsel, Mr. Slobodan Cvijetic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bezbradica. Well, we know your client is on provisional release, and I take it he is aware of this status conference. Do you have anything to report in that context?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. He is aware of everything. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. The last time we had a status conference was towards the end of January, and we then had the prospect of having, according to the work plan, the Prosecution Pre-Trial Brief filed and the Defence Pre-Trial Brief filed. We had at that time one outstanding issue, and that was a motion for adjudicated facts which was filed, I think, in August 2006. So I would say at that time things were looking fairly bright when it came to bringing this case to an end, as far as the pre-trial phase is concerned. And since then, we have indeed had the pre-trial briefs filed, but we also have had some other motions filed, which means that we still have some time to go before we can declare the pre-trial phase over. Let me, before we go over the outstanding motions, and I will offer counsel an opportunity to comment on it and shed whatever light I can on where we are on that, I would like to assure, I think, primarily the Prosecution, but it also concerns the Defence, that the Trial Chamber is very much aware of the fact of the importance of the question of adjudicated facts, well, for two reasons: One is that a resolution of that is of importance for the scope of the Prosecution's case; and the second is, obviously, there's a link to the question of adjudicated facts to the question of agreed facts. The more adjudicated facts that could be agreed between the parties, not only would it have an impact on the scope of the Prosecution's case, but it will have an impact on the matter under dispute which the trial could be concluded. So that's why the Trial Bench will, obviously, try to bring a resolution on the outstanding motions we have there as soon as possible. But at the same time, and I will come back to that, I again would like to urge the parties to take whatever opportunity there is to engage in direct discussion regarding the whole scope of agreed facts. And as I said, I will come back to this point later. This was just, Mr. Tieger, in order to encourage you and your team that that matter is not forgotten. Before we go down to the question of the outstanding motions, I would like to have an understanding to what extent a favourable decision by the Bench on the adjudicated facts motion, as they are now, if you can give me any assistance to what extent that would impact on your need to bring lead witnesses. You know, just give an estimate, if you were favourable on all counts, as far as see them, to what extent would that impact in numbers of witnesses, leaving aside the question of 92 bis and quater for the moment. Is it possible to make an estimate on that, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for many of the purposes of today's hearing, as was the case in the 65 ter yesterday, I'm going to ask Ms. Richterova to take the lead in responding to the Court. And with respect to this particular matter, I'm not sure we're in a position to quantify that precisely for the Court. Certainly, we could indicate to the Court, as a general proposition, that the thrust of the Court's inquiry, at least what I understand to be the thrust of the Court's inquiry, is perfectly correct. There obviously is a relationship between the particular witnesses and number of witnesses the Prosecution would be obliged to call, and the adjudicated facts that may be decided upon. Ms. Richterova may have some more specific information on that that she can relay to the Court; but as I say, at this moment, I'm not in a position to provide the Court with a precise correlation between the adjudicated facts and a favourable ruling on all or a portion of that motion and the precise number of witnesses who would be called, beyond saying that there's a clear relationship between the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Ms. Richterova, anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: At this point, I can add just a little. As you are aware, we filed a second motion for adjudicated facts because the Brdjanin case, the Simic case, and the Galic case have been settled on appeal. We added new facts. They mostly relate to crime-based. So as you can see from these facts, they relate to the ARK region, I would say to five municipalities in the ARK region; further, it relates to Bosanski Sumac and Visegrad. We can reduce significantly the number of witness calling for these municipalities. It doesn't mean, of course, that we won't call any witnesses from these municipalities, but I would like to stress we can reduce their number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Obviously, I had hoped you would say, well, it would cut the case down to two months or something, but I understand the difficulties at this stage to make an assessment. Thank you for what you've given me. Let's now then look at the motions. We have, as far as I can see, three motions on judicial -- adjudicated facts: One from the Defence -- sorry, from the Prosecution, from 2006; and one from the Defence filed early this year on the 1st of February, and those have been responded to, so those are ready, as it were; And then, as Ms. Richterova indicated, we have a very newly-filed motion, filed on the 10th of May. And as you indicated, it's gone by the now final decisions in the Brdjanin, Simic, and Galic cases, and that one needs still to be responded to before the Chamber is ready to deliberate and resolve on it. When would you be ready to respond, Mr. Bezbradica? I am asking because you have indicated that you would have problems meeting the times as it now is laid down. I believe the time would be the 24th of May. Would you be ready to file a response to that at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Your Honour, as you're aware, I just came in from Belgrade last week, Tuesday of last week, and I print out everything from internet on Friday. At this stage, we are still translating the Prosecution motion into the Serbian language, and at this stage everything is under our serious consideration. We will try to reconsider our position and maybe try to make some progress in this way. As I mentioned yesterday, I appreciate if you can give me some extension, not just for this -- my response for this motion, but also for another one or an amended indictment. As you're aware, I go back to my home on Saturday, but I will be retired. I just ask maybe for days, if you can give me. If not, I will do my best to finish everything in due time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bezbradica. We certainly appreciate that coming from down under, as it were, and having to relate with your client in Belgrade, and that puts the stress on you, on a personal base, although the choices that you have undertaken for this assignment, given your domicile, there are obviously limits to the excuses that could be made given that fact. However, I'm not unresponsive, so you are to file a response on the case -- in the matter of the Prosecution's motion for adjudicated facts not later than the 7th of June this year. I added "this year" just to make that clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Moving, then, to, leaving the three motions of adjudicated on the side, next batch, if you will, or motions I have are the two motions from the Defence on access to confidential material: One related to the Mrdja case, and the other to the Deronjic case. And unless you wish to add something on this, Mr. Bezbradica, my intention was only to assure that you we are ready to take a decision on those two motions in the near future.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: I don't have anything. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. There is also, from the Prosecution, a motion on protective measures, a matter which we also will deal with, I hope, in the near future. Any comment from the Prosecution on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I think everything is stated in that motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we have from you, Mr. Bezbradica, two motions dealing with what you perceive to be noncompliance as far as the Prosecution is concerned. The first one regards the question of disclosure of witness statements under Rule 66(A)(II) which you filed on the 23rd of March and a corrigenda to that file on the 30th of April, and it seems to me - I know that this was discussed yesterday at the 65 ter conference as well - that there have been some matters of translation which have delayed the full disclosure from the Prosecution. Is the Prosecution ready to state when a full disclosure of this matter could be had?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As I stated yesterday, we anticipated to disclose 14 of audiotapes with B/C/S translation of certain transcripts, but, unfortunately, today we are faced with a major technical problem. So it has been addressed. It has been almost solved, so I discuss it with Mr. Bezbradica that these 14 transcripts and some additional translations will be disclosed tomorrow morning, and additional they will be disclosed as soon as possible. And if you want to -- if you want me to be more precise, just in case we are facing any other technical problem, one month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Comments, Mr. Bezbradica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: I don't have really any comments, only that I just met a few minutes ago with Ms. Anna to come back tomorrow morning and pick up CDs. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, with those clarifications, I think that matter is ready for a resolution here and now, and in that sense I grant the motion in part by directing the Prosecution to make the full disclosure under 66(A)(II) not later than the 15th of June, which is a Friday, and that should give you your month, Ms. Richterova. And as far as the rest of the motion, that is denied, Mr. Bezbradica. When it comes to the second motion, Mr. Bezbradica, where you argue that the Prosecution is in noncompliance with Rule 65 ter(E), a motion which you filed on the 16th of March, 2007, and with a late corrigendum on the 8th of May, we have had a response to that and the Trial Chamber will take a decision also on that matter in the future. Do you have anything to add to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I don't have. Everything is stated there in my motion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it, by the shaking of the head, nothing from the Prosecution on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You are right, Your Honour, we have nothing more to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. We then come to what was indicated by you, Ms. Richterova; namely, that you also filed simultaneously, more or less, with your motion of adjudicated facts in May, a motion for leave to amend to the rights to amend the indictment on the 9th of May, and I take it from that motion - and I would like to have your confirmation on that - that would not or lead to be granted, change the scope of the indictment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You are right, Your Honour. The reason for filing this proposed amended indictment was primarily to, in light of the recent Brdjanin Appeal Judgement, to reduce the scope of JCE, and also based on the Defence Pre-Trial Brief and his various comments, to clarify the amount of responsibility of his client. There are no new charges included in this proposed second amended indictment, and we are -- we do not intend to call new witnesses or to submit new documents in relation to this proposed amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Mr. Bezbradica, that is also something that needs to be responded to. All I think that Ms. Richterova indicated, some matters there clarified matters that you had raised in the motion that I referred to earlier, but you have indicated that you will not be ready to file a response, which timely would be on the 23rd of May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I would like to ask for an extension for the same reason as earlier. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I had understood that, and you will have the same time as granted for responding to the adjudicated facts motion; that is, on the 7th of June, 2007, we expect to have your response also on the amended indictment motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Well, that exhausts my list of outstanding matters involving the parties. Would that square with the parties' understanding, or are there other matters outstanding as far as motions are concerned?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any additional pending motion or outstanding issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I take it that is your position as well, Mr. Bezbradica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: I think at this stage everything is in proper order, and I am not aware about anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I then come to what I indicated before, the question of agreed facts. As you may recall, I underscored and tried to make that as clear as possible, the Bench appreciation of the parties getting together to agree on matters; not only, as I said, linked to the outstanding motion of adjudicated facts, but also should the parties feel inclined to do so, to cover the whole scope of the case, as such, and only the parties will set the limits for how far agreements can go. And I was a bit disappointed when I understood that despite promises made after the last status conference, there hasn't been - that's my understanding- in a direct context between the Prosecution and the counsel for the Defence on this. I may be wrong, but I wish to have confirmations that regardless of what has happened, in the future parties will now engage in discussions in order to be able to maximize the amount of agreed facts and other matters related to the scope of the case. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm happy to confirm that from the Prosecution's side. We are determined not to let the absence of progress in the past discourage us from engaging in discussions with the Defence towards that end. In light of the past, I'm certainly not going to overstate the likelihood of success, but I will certainly assure the Court that we'll do our best to move that process forward. I can also indicate to the Court that there were discussions with the Defence this week along those very lines, and we'll take on board the Court's suggestion that there's no reason to arbitrarily limit the scope of such discussions, and do everything that can be done to address all issues which may be amenable to agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Mr. Bezbradica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to make some clarification in this regard of agreed facts. As you are aware, the accused agrees to accept the facts under paragraph 25 on page 10 of the current indictment; but in my letter of 13 February 2007, the different advise of the Prosecution that in light of the status conference of the 8th of January, 2007, the accused further agreed to accept the facts under paragraph 29 and 30 on page 11 of the indictment as agreed facts. It means that we have some progress there. At this stage -- or last week I received the proposed second amended indictment and the numbering of paragraphs is slightly changed now, and I'm not sure at this stage what will happen with that indictment. But at this stage we will have new consideration in regard to everything, and we will advise you is there any progress our not. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bezbradica. I'm fully aware that, obviously, you need to seek guidance from your client; but on the other hand, it is you who are the legal expert, and you are the one who is best equipped to assess, for instance, the impact of the Appeals Chambers decisions on cases newly handed down, what that would entail for your client as well, when it comes to assessing the scope of the case as you see it. So it's a two-way street between you and your client. And as I have indicated, I think the broader the discussions could be on what could be agreed between the parties, the better. I think, it would be -- it would be certainly in the interests of justice and in the interests of your client to try to maximise the scope of the field of agreements that could be reached between you and the Prosecution. So with that, I will again underscore the direct contacts between counsel to try to explore, to the extent possible, what could be done here, provided obviously that you bring your client well into the fold in this, Mr. Bezbradica. You're nodding, so I take it you consent.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: I understand everything, Your Honour, and I will advise my client in respect of the conclusion of this status conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bezbradica. I have some matters, before I leave the parties, to raise whatever needs to be raised just to tick off what I have on my list. As far as your work plan is concerned, there are only two outstanding items, and that is the pre-trial conference and the start of the trial. And as the parties are aware, this -- at present this case is scheduled not with an immediate priority; but we also know, and I think the Delic case is an example, that even if scheduling indicates that a case may be some time off to be ready for trial, as far as the Tribunal is concerned, there is a need for the parties to be ready, and that's why this process in order to bring the pre-trial phase to a close is so important. I also understand, Mr. Bezbradica, that you have indicated that you would need something in the order of three months early advanced notice before any trial. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour. I gave my submission yesterday in this respect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we obviously cannot promise, but we have noted your request, and, obviously, we'll take that into account. But some of these matters are, obviously, outside the hands of this Trial Bench when it comes to the planning of the cases for the Tribunal as a whole. With that, it's obviously too early to fill in the blanks when it comes to pre-trial conference and the start of the trial, and that also impacts on the question which also was raised yesterday by you, Ms. Richterova, the question of 92 bis ter and quater statements, and I think you are right, and I think the Defence agrees that the proper Bench to decide on those matters would be the Trial Bench, i.e., the Bench that eventually will hear the case. It also obviously has an impact on the outcome of the pending motions on both adjudicated facts and the motion for leave to amend the indictment. Once those are out of the way, there may also be a need to add to the already-filed pre-trial briefs on both sides; but that would decide, I would imagine, the scope of 92 bis, ter and quater submissions which the Prosecution will make. So what I see is once we have a decision on the outstanding motions, that would be the time for the Prosecution to file motions regarding the written statements, then for the Trial Bench to address that. Would that meet with the parties' understanding? Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I fully agree with you, Your Honour. It makes sense to wait until all the unresolved issues has been resolved, and then we can file our further submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Bezbradica, it's for you to react to each submission from the Prosecution in a timely manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand everything, and once we receive some more we will respond in due time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we have the ongoing matter of Rule 68 disclosures. Are there any things that the parties need to raise here on this, or can I take it that is continually being handled according to usual practice? Mrs. Richterova?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Of course, we are aware of our ongoing obligation, and it is more or less under control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Bezbradica?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Agreed partially. At this stage, I still haven't seen disclosure materials from the Prosecution, but at this stage I haven't seen enough evidence that may suggest the innocence of my client or affect the credibility of the Prosecution witness. But shortly, when I review everything in probably a short period of time, I will address. The Prosecution asked for disclosure of these materials, and we will see what will happen after. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, those are the matters I thought I should raise with the parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I am just reading the transcript. There was something here. I don't fully understand what you mean here. Would you like to comment, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I had the same problem, Your Honour. I want to assume, and I'd like confirmation of the fact, that that's not any kind of allegation by Mr. Bezbradica that the Prosecution is not complying with its Rule 68 obligations by disclosing material that falls within the scope of 68. If it's simply a comment that Mr. Bezbradica hasn't identified himself some kind of material that he would hope to find, then he's welcome to make such comments. But if there is something more to that comment than meets the eye, we would like to know about that because we have been in contact with the Defence about Rule 68, and we weren't aware of any logistical or other disclosure problems in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Bezbradica, one thing is obviously your analysis of the material that you are being provided with by the Prosecution, that's one matter. The other is whether you feel that you are being provided what you have the right to expect. I didn't understand, although it was a bit oblique here, that you made an allegation that the Prosecution didn't provide you with what you are to expect under the disclosure rules, 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: I didn't feel I received plenty of CDs, and when I have time, I'm going to review everything. And at this stage, I haven't reviewed all CDs and all paperwork; and at this stage, I didn't find some information which are going to for the benefit of my client. I didn't feel they are not going to provide me with that; but if I find something that I don't understand or I'm looking for some more information, I will contact them and I will try to fix everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I think that matter is out of the way now. My list is then exhausted. Are there any other matters which the parties need to raise at this point? Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any issues which need to be raised during this status conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Richterova. Mr. Bezbradica?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have any new issues to raise today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, with that, I think we can bring this status conference to a close, and again I encourage parties to engage in vigorous discussions. We are adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference concluded at
